newsitem.title: USA: Brazil offers to swap Brady bonds for 30-yr global.
newsitem.headline: Brazil offers to swap Brady bonds for 30-yr global.

text.p: Brazil on Wednesday offered to to tender selected Brady bonds for cash or to swap selected Bradies for new 30-year uncollaterized, SEC-registered global bonds via Goldman, Sachs and J.P. Morgan.
Brazil also said it would offer its 30-year global bond for cash purchase, and intended to issue at least $1.0 billion of paper through the swap and direct cash purchases.
According to the offer, holders of Brazil Par bonds BR4D24=RR, "C" bonds BR8D14=RR and Discount Z-L bonds BRFLTD24=RR may exchange their paper for global bonds.
Investors may also offer to sell Par and Discount bonds for cash, but the total may not exceed 25 percent of the total amount of Pars and Discounts in the swap.
Also, investors may purchase the global bond for cash, but the total sold for cash may not exceed 25 percent of the total issue.

The Pars will be valued at 2.5 percent over the yield to maturity of the U.S. Treasury bond due November 2026 and the "C" bonds will calculated at 4.6 percent over the yield to maturity of the U.S. Treasury bond due May 2007, both Treasury yields set on the last trading day prior to expiration.
The Discounts value will be fixed at $818.75 per $1,000 face amount.

The global bond will be priced through a modified Dutch auction. Brazil will select a single clearing spread, which, along with the yield of the U.S. Treasury bond due November 2026, will determine the yield and price of the global bonds.
The offer is scheduled to expire at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT on June 3, unless extended or ended earlier by Brazil. Results will be announced on the following business day.
